prompt: Extract every valid email address from input.html. Normalize to lowercase. End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {emails: string[]}.
Read input.txt and extract every real calendar date mentioned. Normalize to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {dates: string[]}.

Read input.txt (a coffee-shop receipt). Extract every transaction line as {label, amount_usd}. Discounts are negative. Skip lines that aren't real transactions: ad copy, struck-through staff notes, footer notices, tip-jar mentions. End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {transactions: [{label: string, amount_usd: number}]}.

Read input.md (an academic excerpt) and extract every external citation. For each, return {authors: string[], year: number, title: string}. Use just the author surnames (e.g. ['Lewis'] or ['Nogueira', 'Cho']) — do NOT include 'et al.' as a name. Each citation appears once even if mentioned multiple times. Skip internal references (section numbers, naked years without an author, citations without a title). End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {citations: [{authors: string[], year: number, title: string}]}.

Read CHANGELOG.md and extract every released version. A 'release' is a version that appears as the heading of a release section (e.g. '## [1.6.0] - 2026-04-12'). Skip the Unreleased section, body-text mentions of versions (e.g. '1.5.x', '2.0.0-rc.1'), and the reserved smoke-test version. End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {versions: string[]}.

Read input.html (a marketing newsletter) and extract every CONTENT url — links to articles, docs, videos, careers pages, etc. Skip tracking infrastructure: unsubscribe / manage-preferences / open-tracker / 1x1 pixel / view-in-browser links (anything on the email.tracker.example or cdn.tracker.example hostnames). End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {urls: string[]}.

Read input.csv and extract every data row as an object keyed by column name (name, role, city, salary). Header is on line 1. Handle quoted fields with embedded commas, doubled-quotes for literal quotes, blank fields (use ""), trailing commas, and skip wholly-empty rows. Salary stays as a string (don't coerce to number). End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {rows: [{name: string, role: string, city: string, salary: string}]}.

Read input.txt (an internal email about office moves) and extract every active deliverable postal address as {street, city, region, postal, country}. Use empty string "" for fields that don't apply (e.g. some countries don't use a region). SKIP: vacated / explicitly-excluded addresses, P.O. boxes without a city, anything that isn't a real street address. End your reply with a fenced ```json``` block matching the schema {addresses: [{street, city, region, postal, country}]}.
